newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: New black S.African investment group launched.
newsitem.headline: New black S.African investment group launched.

text.p: A new black-owned South African investment holding company with a capital base of about 275 million rand and plans to list on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange was launched on Monday.
Representing 300,000 large and small black investors throughout South Africa, the National Empowerment Corporation (NE Corp) is an offshoot of the National Empowerment Consortium.

NE Corp chairman Mashudu Ramano said in a statement the aim would not be to compete with other investment groupings such as New Africa Investment's Ltd or Worldwide Africa Investment Holdings (Pty) Ltd, but to focus on growth ventures in which it could obtain meaningful stakes.
It already has an 8.7 percent stake in Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd and holdings in a Durban-based manufacturing company and African Heritage Asset Managers.
NE Corp was formed in June last year and management have undertaken a national roadshow to encourage black business groups, including teacher and taxi associations, to join it.
"The focus in the next two years will fall on growing businesses in the industrial, financial services, printing and retail sectors," Ramano said.
